notes: SUPERSEDED BY THE PROMOTION. Original text: 'Manually curated against include/daObjRc_Dorifu_c.h; the class TU contains real member definitions and one empty destructor definition rather than the legacy C D0 body.' The empty destructor definition is exactly what the promotion removed -- see the PROMOTION note below. What remains true is that the manifest was curated by hand against the header.

SUPERSEDED BY THE PROMOTION, in every clause. Original text: 'STRICT PARTIAL-ISOLATION BOUNDARY: D1, InitResources, and CleanupResources are contribution-identical. Compiler-generated D0 calls __cxa_vec_cleanup while the legacy C object names the configured same-address alias __destroy_arr (both arm9 0x0207328c), so symbolic object equivalence is conservatively 3/4 and no partial-link claim is made.' There is no compiler-generated D0 any more -- D0 is a hand-transcribed mangled body that names __destroy_arr explicitly, so the divergence the note was about no longer exists -- and there is no legacy C object, and the range is now five functions rather than four.

PROMOTION (read this first). Before the promotion this TU carried a real `daObjRc_Dorifu_c::~daObjRc_Dorifu_c()` member and verified 4/4 MATCH with objisolate clean -- but with `emission order: 1 ordinal pair(s) NOT in ROM order: [(0, 1)]` and an unhomed `_ZN16daObjRc_Dorifu_cD2Ev` that no ROM address claims. The cartridge keeps D1 at 0x02111f8c BELOW D0 at 0x0211200c while mwccarm emits the D2/D1/D0 group D0-then-D1, so production isolation would have refused it. Both variants are now `// @symbol` mangled bodies transcribed from the cartridge with tools/disasm.py (ov036 base 0x021111a0); D2 is gone and the order line now reads `all 5 function(s) in the expected ROM-ascending section order`. That costs the CONVERTED tier's no-raw-offset and no-mangled-refs criteria for those two functions, banked in config/converted-backslide-exceptions.jsonl. The TU also absorbed daObjRc_Dorifu_c_classInit at 0x021120c8, which was contiguous with the other four and previously stood alone; the section now runs .text 0x02111f8c-0x02112158. NO VPTR BIAS: symbols.txt records _ZTV16daObjRc_Dorifu_c at 0x02113ecc and that IS the address point -- D1's literal pool word at 0x02111ff8 is exactly 0x02113ecc -- so every vptr store names the symbol with addend 0.

WHY THE DESTRUCTOR IS DECLARED LAST IN include/daObjRc_Dorifu_c.h, and where the 13 compiler_only_output entries come from. Nothing defines ~daObjRc_Dorifu_c() as a C++ member (see the previous note), so the class's vtable and RTTI have no key function to home them. Whether mwccarm emits them here turns on WHERE the destructor is declared in the class body: measured on the sibling daObjWc_Mizu_c, declared FIRST the TU emits 0 data symbols, moved after the other members it emits the full set. Declared first is not harmless -- it drops _ZTI/_ZTS/_ZTV16daObjRc_Dorifu_c out of the set of ROM data any source verifies, and tools/validate_merge.py ratchets on that count with no escape hatch. The 13 licensed entries are this class's own three plus the vague-linkage RTTI passengers of the base chain daObjDorifu_c / dBgActor_c / dActor_c / fBase_c / dBase_c -- a longer chain than the daObjWc_* siblings' because this class sits two levels below dBgActor_c.

The three remaining `objisolate: _ZTV16daObjRc_Dorifu_c: unexpected reloc type=2 addend=0` DIFFs on D1, D0 and classInit are a verify-path artifact, not a defect. tools/objisolate.py demands `addend >= VTABLE_PREAMBLE` only for a _ZTV symbol it is EXTERNALISING; in production the deadstrip-data disposition drops it instead, where addend 0 is the correct spelling. The same command run against the already-landed, CI-green src/actors/d_a_obj_wc_mizu.cpp and src/actors/d_a_obj_wc_obj03.cpp produces the identical shape. tools/rombuild.py -j16 is the gate that matters.
